picks.excerpt: Google researchers demonstrated a quantum processor that uses reinforcement learning to learn from its own error-correction data mid-computation, continuously recalibrating the hardware without pausing the run. The approach cut logical error rates about 20% beyond conventional calibration and kept performance 3.5x more stable under hardware drift on the Willow chip.
picks.rationale: AI folded into quantum error correction on Google's Willow chip — reinforcement learning that self-recalibrates mid-run is a concrete method advance for fault-tolerant computing.

picks.excerpt: A hybrid quantum-classical AI pipeline designed immune-targeting peptides, with quantum-generated inputs showing particular promise for understudied genetic variants that lack enough data to train classical models alone. It is an early demonstration of quantum-assisted generative modeling feeding real immunology design.
picks.rationale: Quantum-assisted generative AI feeding real immunology design — notable for helping data-poor genetic variants where classical models alone fall short.

picks.excerpt: University of Manchester researchers built a physics-informed machine-learning method that screened more than 10,000 candidate 2D materials for rare 'flat-band' electronic states tied to magnetism, unconventional superconductivity and topological behavior. The model confirmed flat-band behavior with 98.2% accuracy, published in Science Advances.
picks.rationale: Physics-informed ML screening 10,000+ 2D materials at 98.2% accuracy shows how AI compresses the materials-discovery search space for exotic quantum states.

picks.excerpt: Aalto University researchers used a machine-learning-guided search to identify new kagome-lattice superconductors YRu3B2 and LuRu3B2, narrowing the vast materials space that has to be tested experimentally. The work is part of the broader AI-driven hunt for room-temperature superconductors.
picks.rationale: ML-guided search that surfaced two new kagome superconductors is a tangible win in the AI-driven hunt for better superconducting materials.

picks.excerpt: In a PNAS study, TU Dresden researchers combined behavioral experiments with participants' own free-text explanations, analyzed by large language models, to uncover the hidden reasons behind human decisions. It shows LLMs can extract cognitive insight from open-ended text that choice data alone cannot capture, a new tool for cognitive science.
picks.rationale: LLMs mining free-text explanations to reveal why people decide as they do — a genuinely new method for cognitive science that choice data alone can't reach.
